expect_always.empty_mask:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: expect_always: the condition constrains no bits of 0x600, so every frame satisfies it and the invariant is true however the firmware behaves.
  Name the signals that must hold with   signals: { <signal>: <value> }.
  An unconstrained expect_can is a real claim -- that a frame with this id arrived at all -- but an unconstrained invariant is a claim about nothing.

expect_boots.node_declares_no_banner:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'updater' declares no boot_text in the topology, so there is nothing that would prove it came back.
  Add   boot_text: "<the line this firmware prints once it is up>"   to that node in the topology file.
  The engine must not guess: a boot check that matched nothing would pass the moment the window closed, and a bricked device would read as a healthy one.
expect_boots.node_is_scripted: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' is a frame player, so there is nothing to boot. A player has no firmware and never says anything it was not scripted to say.

expect_flash.node_is_scripted: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' is a frame player and has no memory to read. This verb is for executed nodes only.

expect_order.sequence_entry_not_a_mapping: test-scenario.yml: step 1: expect_order: entry 1 of 'sequence' is the text '0x600', not a mapping. Each entry describes one frame, the same way expect_can does: an id, and optionally the signals that narrow it.
expect_order.sequence_not_a_list:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: expect_order: 'sequence' is the ordered list of frames, so it must be a list. It is a mapping.
  Write it as   sequence: [ { id: ..., signals: {...} }, { id: ..., signals: {...} } ]   with the entries in the order they must first appear.
expect_order.sequence_too_short:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: expect_order: 'sequence' has 1 entry, and an order needs at least two things to be in.
  For a single frame, use   expect_can: { id: ..., within_ms: ... }   which is the verb for that.

expect_symbol.node_is_scripted: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' has no firmware behind it, so it has no memory to read

flood.count_not_positive: test-scenario.yml: step 1: count must be positive, got 0

mark.text_missing: test-scenario.yml: step 1: needs the text to record

node_freeze.board_names_no_core:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: board 'bms_ecu' does not name the core, so there is nothing to halt.
  Add   cpu_peripheral: <name>   to that board in test-boards.yml.
  The engine must not guess what a core is called on a customer's part: a guess that resolved to nothing would halt nothing, and the scenario would still report PASS.
node_freeze.node_is_scripted:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' is a frame player, and 'node_freeze' halts a core that is executing firmware. There is no core behind a player to halt.
  To take this node off the bus, use   node_silence: { node: motor, silence: true }   which works on either kind of node.
  To model a hung ECU here, give the node firmware (type: real) in the topology file. No scenario changes.

node_resume.board_names_no_core:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: board 'bms_ecu' does not name the core, so there is nothing to halt.
  Add   cpu_peripheral: <name>   to that board in test-boards.yml.
  The engine must not guess what a core is called on a customer's part: a guess that resolved to nothing would halt nothing, and the scenario would still report PASS.
node_resume.node_is_scripted:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' is a frame player, and 'node_resume' halts a core that is executing firmware. There is no core behind a player to halt.
  To take this node off the bus, use   node_silence: { node: motor, silence: true }   which works on either kind of node.
  To model a hung ECU here, give the node firmware (type: real) in the topology file. No scenario changes.

node_signal.no_signal_symbols:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'bms' is executed as firmware, so this verb writes the globals behind those signals, and the topology binds none.
  Add   signal_symbols: { <signal>: <symbol>, ... }   to that node in the topology file.
  Nothing in the scenario changes.
node_signal.node_does_not_emit: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' does not emit 0x200, so there is no payload to change
node_signal.signal_not_bound: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'vcu' binds no symbol for signal 'not_a_bound_signal'. Bound signals: drive_state
node_signal.signals_missing: test-scenario.yml: step 1: needs 'signals' with at least one entry

power_cut.board_names_no_core: test-scenario.yml: step 1: board 'ota_ecu' does not name the core, so there is nothing to stop. Add   cpu_peripheral: <name>   to that board in test-boards.yml.
power_cut.board_names_no_ram:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: board 'ota_ecu' declares no RAM regions, so a power cut here would wipe nothing and leave every byte of state intact across it.
  Add   ram_regions: [{ base: <hex>, size: <hex> }, ...]   to that board in test-boards.yml.
  The engine must not guess where a customer's part keeps its RAM: a guess that wiped nothing would turn every power_cut into a warm reset, and the scenario would still report PASS.
power_cut.node_is_scripted:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' is a frame player, so it has no power to cut. There is no core, no RAM and no flash behind a player.
  To model a device losing power here, give the node firmware (type: real) in the topology file. No scenario changes.

power_restore.board_names_no_core: test-scenario.yml: step 1: board 'ota_ecu' does not name the core, so there is nothing to start. Add   cpu_peripheral: <name>   to that board in test-boards.yml.
power_restore.board_names_no_reset_vector:
test-scenario.yml: step 1: board 'ota_ecu' does not say where its reset vector is, so this device cannot be told where to start.
  Add   reset_vector_address: <hex>   to that board in test-boards.yml.
  On an ordinary Cortex-M part that is the start of flash. The engine must not guess: a guessed address that pointed at nothing would halt the core, and a halted core is indistinguishable from a device that was genuinely bricked -- which is the one thing this verb exists to measure.
power_restore.node_is_scripted: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' is a frame player, so it has no power to restore. There is no core behind a player to start.

wait_uart.node_is_scripted: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' has no firmware behind it, so it has no console to wait on

write_symbol.node_is_scripted: test-scenario.yml: step 1: node 'motor' has no firmware behind it, so it has no memory to write into. This verb is for executed nodes only
